title: Veld Project Configuration (v3)
description: Any Veld config file. All top-level keys are optional except in the root config (veld.json or veld.jsonc — both are read, and both in one directory is an error), which must declare schemaVersion and name — so one schema covers the root file and every file it includes, and $schema autocompletion works in all of them.

$schema.description: Optional JSON Schema reference for editor autocompletion. Note: veld accepts JSONC (comments and trailing commas) in every config file, but editors validate a .json file with a strict JSON parser — name the root file veld.jsonc, or map veld.json to the 'jsonc' language in your editor, to stop spurious syntax errors.

schemaVersion.description: Required in the root config file only. Must be "3" — v1 and v2 are not supported and fail to load. In v3 the `command` key is gone: every place that runs something uses `argv` (an array, spawned directly) or `shell` (a string, run via sh -c). See docs/migrating-to-v3.md to convert an older config.

name.description: Required in the root config file only. Human-readable project name, used in URLs and run history.

include.description: Globs of further config files to load, relative to this file's directory. Root config only — nested includes are refused, because load order (and so error messages) would depend on a graph nobody can see. Matches are loaded in sorted order. `*` matches within one path segment, `?` one character, `**` across segments.

url_template.description: Hostname template for start_server nodes. Uses {variable} — single braces — not ${variable}.

vars.description: One definition point per value, referenced as ${vars.<name>} at every use site. A var is a scalar or a single value source — never an object, never a config fragment: the key stays written in the node that uses it, so `rg <ENV_VAR>` still finds the line that sets it. A var may not reference another var (one hop, always). A literal may use the run-scoped built-ins (${veld.run}, run_id, name, project, root, worktree, branch, username); the per-node ones (port, url, url.*, ports.*, node, variant) are a lint error here, because a var is one value for the whole run — compose those at the use site. A var backed by a value source is resolved only when the resolved plan reaches it, so a credential helper behind a var costs nothing on a run that does not use it.

env.description: Project-wide environment variables, inherited by every node variant.

presets.description: Named selections for `veld start --preset <name>`. An entry starting with @ references another preset, so overlapping sets need not repeat every selection. Cycles are an error.

setup.description: Steps run sequentially before the dependency graph. A non-zero exit aborts startup.

teardown.description: Steps run sequentially after all nodes stop. Best-effort: failures are logged, never blocking.

nodes.description: The dependency graph. A node is defined in exactly one file — the same name in two files is an error naming both, which is what removes precedence rules for node bodies entirely.

hooks.description: RESERVED. Repo-declared lifecycle hooks keyed by event (worktree.created, project.created, run.stopped). Parsed and stored but NOT EXECUTED by this version of veld — `veld lint` says so. Hooks are not nodes: no graph, no port, no probes. Repo-declared only, never from a fetched extension.

ui.description: RESERVED. JSON-defined UI extensions for the desktop app. Parsed and stored but NOT RENDERED by this version of veld.

value.description: A value: a plain string (a non-secret literal), or an object naming exactly one source plus an optional `secret` flag. veld never takes custody of a secret — it carries a pointer and a flag, resolves it at run start, and passes it to the process's environment or a file. Nothing here names a vendor: `argv` runs a command and reads stdout, and which command that is is your business.
An inline literal. This object form exists so a literal can carry `secret: true`.

env.description: Read from the environment veld was launched with. Missing at start is an error naming the node and the variable.

file.description: Read the (trimmed) contents of a file. Relative to the project root.

argv.description: Run a command directly and take its trimmed stdout.

shell.description: Run a shell command and take its trimmed stdout.

secretFlag.description: Declares the value sensitive: masked in output, encrypted at rest, scrubbed from the share payload, and REFUSED where veld would interpolate it into an argv element or shell string (both appear in the process table). A bare $NAME inside a shell string or an `sh -c` script is fine and is the recommended form — the shell expands it at runtime in the child, so it never enters argv; so is handing a container the name only, ["docker", "run", "-e", "NAME", "img"]. A secret's sanctioned destinations are the process environment and a file.

envMap.description: Environment variables. Additive across project → node → variant, with the most specific level winning per key; a level erases an inherited key by setting it to null.

oneOf.description: Erase this key inherited from a less specific level.

argv.description: An argument vector, spawned directly: no shell, no word splitting, no globbing. Interpolation runs per element after the array is fixed, so a value containing spaces, globs, quotes, or newlines can never change the argument count.

commandObject.description: Something to run: exactly one of `argv` or `shell`.

shell.description: Run via sh -c; you own the quoting. Permanently supported — any node that misbehaves under argv can be reverted to a string with no veld change and no config version change.

failureMessage.description: Shown when the step exits non-zero. Useful for prerequisite checks.

portSpec.description: How a named port is obtained.

oneOf.description: A fixed port. Discouraged: a literal port silently breaks parallel worktrees, which is the reason named auto-ports exist. veld will not substitute a different one if it is taken.

portsMap.description: Named ports veld allocates, referenced as ${veld.ports.<name>} and exported as VELD_PORT_<NAME>. ${veld.port} remains the primary — the one named `http`, or the sole entry. Omit entirely for the historical behaviour: one allocated port.

filesMap.description: Values delivered to disk before the process starts, for a program that can only read a file. Paths are relative to the project root; parent directories are created; the file is created WITH its mode (default 0600) rather than chmod-ed afterwards, so a credential is never briefly world-readable.

oneOf.description: A value plus an optional octal mode.

mode.description: Octal file mode as a string, e.g. "0600". A string, not a number, because a bare number has already lost its leading zero.

dependsOn.description: Dependencies: node name → variant name. Both must be written LITERALLY — no ${…}. The graph is read before any variable exists, so an interpolated dependency would need a two-stage evaluator. Additive over the node level; "node": null erases an inherited dependency.

stepType.description: `command` runs to completion; `start_server` stays running and gets an allocated port and a URL. These are the only two primitives.

clientLogLevels.description: Browser console levels to capture. 'exception' is always captured.

features.description: Per-field cascade: project → node → variant, most specific wins field by field.

feedback_overlay.description: Inject the Veld toolbar into HTML responses.

inject.description: Inject bootstrap scripts automatically. When false the /__veld__/* routes still exist for manual script tags.

set.description: Header name -> value. Plain strings only: these values travel to Caddy and to the public gateway as part of a route, so the value-source/`secret` forms are NOT yet supported here. Do not put a credential in a header value — see the follow-up noted in docs/configuration.md.

proxy.description: Static header manipulation by the local proxy and the public gateway. Resolvable at project, node, and variant level: `remove` lists union case-insensitively, `set` maps override per key, and a header in both is resolved in favour of `set`.

probe.description: A readiness or liveness check. A variant REPLACES an inherited probe wholesale rather than merging into it — a probe is a tagged union, so field-wise merging would let a variant switch type from http to command and silently inherit a stale path.

port.description: READINESS ONLY. Which named port from `ports` to check; default is the primary. A multi-port node's readiness is rarely 'any port is open' — a debugger port opens long before the app is listening. Not yet supported on a liveness probe, which always watches the primary port.

failure_threshold.description: Liveness only: consecutive failures before recovery. Default 3.

max_recoveries.description: Liveness only: recovery attempts before permanent failure. Default 3.

readiness.description: Gates the dependency graph during startup. A start_server without one is reported healthy as soon as its port opens, so dependents start before it can serve. null erases an inherited probe.

liveness.description: Runs continuously after the node is healthy; triggers recovery. null erases an inherited probe.

outputs.description: Values this node publishes, referenced elsewhere as ${nodes.<node>.<KEY>}. A list declares names captured from the node's own output; a map publishes computed values (available on both node types — on a `command` node the map is interpolated after the command runs, with its captured outputs in scope, so a build step can say where its artifact landed). Replaced wholesale by a variant; null erases.

share.description: Per-service sharing opt-in. Absent, or an empty `expose`, means this service can never be shared. Replaced wholesale by a variant rather than merged — sharing is a consent decision and a half-inherited expose list is exactly the surprise it must not have. null erases.

access.description: Viewer access for the public URL. Default: password — never an open URL by accident.

action.description: A user-invokable command on a node, exposed as `veld action <name>` and as a dashboard button.

parameters.description: Static values available as ${param.KEY} and as environment variables. Plain strings only — the value-source/`secret` forms are not yet supported here.

requires_outputs.description: Output keys that must all be present for this action to be available.

node.description: A node and its variants. Any variant field may be declared once here, at node level, and any variant may override it — this deduplicates VALUES, never structure: which keys a node has is still written in that node. There is no inheritance, no mixins, no templates.

hidden.description: Hide from `veld nodes`. Still participates in the graph.

cwd.description: Relative to the PROJECT ROOT, not to the file that declares it.

on_stop.description: Default teardown hook for every variant of this node, run in reverse dependency order during `veld stop`. A variant replaces it, or erases it with `"on_stop": null`. `null` here is simply equivalent to omitting the key — accepted because serde accepts it, and a schema stricter than the parser flags configs that load fine. It receives every ${veld.*} the node itself had, the URL family and named ports included, so a resource named after the same built-ins in argv and here cannot drift.

variant.description: One way to run a node. `type` and the command may come from the node level instead. Exactly one of argv or shell.

script.description: Path to a script file, relative to the project root. An alternative to argv/shell.

cwd.description: Relative to the PROJECT ROOT, not to the file that declares it.

health_check.description: Deprecated alias for probes.readiness. Still accepted.

sensitive_outputs.description: Output keys whose values are sensitive: masked in display, encrypted at rest. Must all be declared in `outputs`.

strict_outputs.description: Fail if the command produces an output not declared in `outputs`. Cannot be null.

skip_if.description: Idempotency check: skip this step if the command exits 0.

on_stop.description: Teardown, run in reverse dependency order during `veld stop`. `null` erases a hook inherited from the node level (and nothing runs); omitting the key inherits it. It receives every ${veld.*} this variant had at start — for a start_server that includes ${veld.url}, ${veld.url.*} and ${veld.ports.*} — plus ${output.KEY} and ${vars.*}, so a resource named after the same built-ins in argv and here cannot drift.

verify.description: Deprecated alias for `skip_if`, still accepted. Prefer `skip_if`.

secretSource.description: Where a token is read from. A plain string is a literal (convenient locally, but it lands in version control).

sharing.description: Environment-wide sharing policy. Relays must be opted into explicitly — including public — so nothing is routed over public relays by accident.

oneOf.description: Self-hosted relays. Share traffic is confined to these.

dangerouslyEmbedRelayTokensInTicket.description: DANGER. Embeds the resolved relay token in every share link. Only for disposable, per-project tokens you rotate freely.
